scope: Static implementation review; no credentials accessed and no live API validation performed.

findings.bug: Duplicates within a returned page are never compared with one another. A first page containing the same record twice and total=2 is accepted as complete despite only one distinct article.
findings.test: Return two identical ART IDs within page 1, total=2. Assert a duplicate/inconsistent status, no page advancement and no false complete.

findings.bug: Cross-page overlap detection uses whole record dictionaries including XML. The same article ID with altered whitespace, attribute ordering, provider verification or updated metadata is accepted as a different article, allowing missing articles to be hidden by duplicate counts.
findings.test: Page 1 and page 2 return the same article-id with different title/XML formatting, total=2. Assert overlap by stable article identity. Repeat for referenceSearch using its verified schema-specific identifier.

findings.bug: Positive totals smaller than the returned or cumulative record count are not rejected. Completion uses >= total, so total=1 with ten records is declared complete and persisted as valid.
findings.test: Test total=1 with ten unique records and a later page that overshoots the remaining total. Assert inconsistent_response and preserve the last accepted checkpoint.

findings.bug: int() is used only to validate pagination, while original values are serialized. displayCount=1.5 or page=True pass validation but send non-integral wire values, which can trigger server defaults and obscure the observed 1-request/10-return anomaly.
findings.test: Reject fractional floats and booleans, or normalize only accepted canonical integer inputs before URL serialization. Assert query values actually transmitted.

pagination_validation_requirements: Returning ten records for displayCount=1 alone does not establish a pagination bug: an effective default size may be used consistently. Compare stable IDs for requested sizes 1, 10 and 20 on pages 1 and 2, recording requested and observed counts.

Verify page 2 differs from page 1; verify ordered concatenation of two ten-record pages against a twenty-record page where the endpoint supports it. An unchanged total alone does not prove an unchanged result set.

Test a 21-record fixed-size response sequence 10/10/1 with requested size 1, interruption after page 1, and resume at page 2. Require 21 unique IDs and exact completion without deriving next_page from requested size.
Test ignored page parameters returning the same IDs, changing totals, empty premature pages, short non-final pages, and max_pages exhaustion followed by resume.

Resume currently trusts stored query/status/count/page contents and returns completed checkpoints without revalidation. Add checkpoint consistency checks if resumable integrity is part of the contract, and explicitly record that same-total live dataset drift cannot be fully ruled out without snapshot support.
existing_test_gap: The sole collection test uses synthetic title-only records and one item per page. It does not exercise provider identifiers, server-default page sizes, duplicate pages, count overshoot, or result-set drift.
